Off the field · Sue's story

## Why we play.

Founded and led by Stephen Epathite, Sue's Angels FC was built on football, friendship and togetherness, honouring the life and memory of Susan Anne Martin.

Following Sue's passing from sepsis in 2020, the club raises awareness through charity matches and community initiatives, keeping her memory at the heart of everything.

[Learn the signs](https://sepsistrust.org/)

### Discipline

Standards on and off the pitch. Earn the shirt every week.

02

### Brotherhood

A football family bound by respect and resilience.

03

### Remembrance

Everything we do honours the memory of Susan Anne Martin.

04

### Ambition

Champions in year one. We look ahead with hunger.

## Player of the Month

![](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/badge/sue-angels-shield.webp)

Player of the Month

March · 25/26

### Daniel McLane

Congratulations to Dan on being named Sue's Angels FC Player of the Month for March, making it two awards in a row after also winning in February.

Dan continued his outstanding season with a series of influential performances from centre-back. Despite playing in defence, he contributed an impressive 4 goals, helped the team keep 3 clean sheets, and picked up a Man of the Match award along the way.

His leadership, consistency and quality at both ends of the pitch were key as Sue's Angels FC went through March unbeaten, making this latest accolade thoroughly deserved.

Congratulations, Dan!

View profile

Share

25/26 awards night

## End of Season Awards

![](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/badge/sue-angels-shield.webp)

Top Assister

### Charlie Dunkley

Relentless all season. Energy, intelligence and selfless running made him a constant threat, and his assists and link play drove our attacking success.

![](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/badge/sue-angels-shield.webp)

Defensive Record Award

### Luke Munns

The goalkeeper every championship side needs. Calm, commanding and full of match-winning saves as the Angels set a historic defensive record.

![](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/badge/sue-angels-shield.webp)

Goal of the Season

### Malachi Mullings

A stunning strike against Mala Vida, pure quality. A huge part of the season before injury cut it short. We can’t wait to see him back in yellow.

![](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/badge/sue-angels-shield.webp)

Top Goalscorer

### Frazier-Isaías Osunkoya

Goals, goals and more goals. Movement, composure and a finish in him at any moment. When the team needed one, Fraizer usually delivered.

![](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/badge/sue-angels-shield.webp)

Clubman of the Year

### Jim El Bayati

A leader, role model and true club servant. As he closes his playing career he leaves the culture and standards that drive the club. A true legend.

![](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/badge/sue-angels-shield.webp)

Players’ Player of the Year

### Daniel McLane

Voted for by his teammates. Solid as a rock in defence and a real weapon from set pieces. A warrior who set the standard every single week.

![](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/badge/sue-angels-shield.webp)

Manager’s Player of the Year

### Dean Knight

Consistency, versatility and constant improvement. Right-back, wing-back, even emergency keeper with two clean sheets. Whatever the team needed, Dean delivered.

# For _Sue_.

Sue’s Angels FC was founded in memory of Susan Anne Martin, who we lost to sepsis. We play in her name, and we hope that by sharing what we have learned, we can help other families recognise the signs in time.

Know the signs Donate in her memory

**2025** Founded in her memory

**48,000** Lives lost to sepsis in the UK each year

**6** Signs that can help save one

Why we exist

> “What we do in life echoes in eternity.”

Everything about this club begins with one person. Sue’s Angels FC was founded in 2025 in memory of Susan Anne Martin, so that her name stays part of something good, week after week.

We lost Sue to sepsis. It is a loss her family and friends carry every day, and it is the reason this club exists. We play for her, and we talk openly about sepsis so that fewer people have to go through the same thing.

![Sue’s Angels FC players together](https://www.suesangelsfc.co.uk/assets/hero/banner-04.jpg)

Understanding sepsis

## What sepsis is

Sepsis is what can happen when the body’s response to an infection starts to harm its own tissues and organs. It can affect anyone, at any age, and it can turn serious very quickly. That is why noticing it early matters so much.

The [UK Sepsis Trust](https://www.sepsistrust.org/) estimates that sepsis takes around 48,000 lives in the UK every year. So many of those losses could have been prevented, and the biggest difference is spotting it early. That is why we keep talking about it.

Know the signs

## Could it be sepsis?

In an adult, trust your instinct and get help quickly. Call 999 or NHS 111, and ask the question if you notice any of these:

### Slurred speech or confusion

Sudden disorientation, drowsiness or trouble speaking clearly.

### Extreme shivering or muscle pain

Shaking, fever, or pain that feels far worse than usual.

### Passing no urine in a day

A clear drop in how often they go to the toilet.

### Severe breathlessness

Struggling for breath, or breathing very fast.

### “It feels like I’m going to die”

A deep, sudden sense that something is seriously wrong.

### Skin mottled, bluish or pale

Blotchy, discoloured or unusually pale skin.

In a child or baby

Call 999 or go straight to A&E if a child:

- Is breathing very fast
- Has a fit or convulsion
- Looks mottled, bluish or pale
- Has a rash that doesn’t fade when you press it
- Is very lethargic or hard to wake
- Feels abnormally cold to touch

For babies under 5, also look out for not feeding, repeated vomiting, or no wet nappy for 12 hours.

Trust your instinct. If someone is getting worse quickly, please do not wait. Ask the question: could it be sepsis?

This is general guidance. For full, up to date information, please visit the [UK Sepsis Trust](https://www.sepsistrust.org/) and the [NHS](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/sepsis/).

Get involved

## Three ways to help

### Know and share the signs

The signs above can save a life. Take a moment to learn them, and share them with the people you love.

Share this page

### Support the UK Sepsis Trust

The UK Sepsis Trust offers support to families, funds research, and raises awareness across the country. You can find out more or give on their website.

[Visit sepsistrust.org](https://www.sepsistrust.org/)

### Stand with the club

Back Sue’s Angels as a sponsor, partner or volunteer, and help us carry her message a little further.
